title: Normalized ideal-power Rees cohomology data on an algebraic space
statement: Let $A$ be a commutative ring, $I\subseteq A$ an ideal, $X$ an algebraic space over $\operatorname{Spec} A$ [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-affine-spectrum, def-trf-algebraic-space], and $F$ a module sheaf on its small etale ringed site [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. Use the pullback $a_T$ of a base element on a chart $T$ from [def-sfb-space-ideal-power-quotients]. An ideal-power Rees cohomology datum in degree $q\in\mathbb N$ consists of module sheaves $G_r$, maps $i_r:G_r\to F$ injective on every chart, and maps $\lambda_{k,r}(a):G_r\to G_{r+k}$ for $a\in I^k$. Require that the range of $i_r$ on every chart $T$ consists exactly of sections $s$ for which some covering sieve $R$ of $T$ has $s|_V\in\langle a_Vt:a\in I^r,t\in F(V)\rangle_{\mathcal O_X(V)}$ for every arrow $V\to T$ of $R$. Thus $G_r$ is precisely the locally generated $(I\mathcal O_X)^rF$, including $G_0=F$ via its inclusion. Require $i_{r+k}(\lambda_{k,r}(a)(s))=a_Ti_r(s)$ on every chart. Compute the actual cohomology $H_r=H^q(X,G_r)$ of underlying additive sheaves [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology] by restriction to the equivalent small affine etale model [def-sfb-space-small-ringed-model] and Mathlib sheaf cohomology, with Ext in the section universe $u$ (as for the graded finiteness input lem-sfb-space-graded-cohomology-finite). The datum also includes $A$-module structures on $H_r$ such that $H^q(\lambda_{0,r}(a))(x)=ax$ for every $a\in I^0=A$, and each $H^q(\lambda_{k,r}(a))$ is $A$-linear. Finally it includes a module structure over $\mathcal R_A(I)$ [def-nagata-rees-algebra] on the additive direct sum $\bigoplus_r H_r$, with action $b\cdot x=\sum_{k\in\operatorname{supp}b}\sum_{r\in\operatorname{supp}x}\operatorname{in}_{r+k}H^q(\lambda_{k,r}(b_k))(x_r)$ for every polynomial $b=\sum b_kt^k$ in that Rees algebra and every finite-support vector $x$. Its degree-zero action satisfies $(a t^0)\operatorname{in}_r(x)=\operatorname{in}_r(ax)$. All cohomology maps here are those of the fixed additive-sheaf cohomology functor. No existence or finiteness assertion is part of this definition.
